name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with only 22B engaged per token, cutting compute cost by ~40% versus flat 70B models while matching or beating their output quality. The trade-off is higher memory bandwidth demand—MoE layers shuffle experts per token, so we need faster RAM or sharding to avoid stalls.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s MoE routing overhead isn’t the only latency killer—Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct just failed a live test (404 on both model IDs), proving model access is fragile. A safer play is DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct: it’s proven stable, beats flat 70B models on quality, and avoids MoE’s memory spikes—run a 10k-token latency benchmark to settle it.

Adopt DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. It delivers 671B total parameters with only 67B active per token, cutting compute cost by ~30% versus flat 70B models while outperforming them on quality benchmarks. The trade-off is higher memory bandwidth demand—MoE models like this need fast RAM to feed their wide active layers—but DeepSeek’s routing is stable and proven in production, unlike the broken Llama-3.3-70B.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct’s MoE routing still adds latency—benchmarks show ~15-20% slower than flat 70B models on EXCAVA’s hardware. Use Llama-3.2-90B-Instruct instead: stable access, flat 90B parameters, no MoE overhead, and it beats DeepSeek on quality in recent evals. Run a 24-hour stability test with identical prompts—if it stays live and faster, it wins.
